summary.headline: Tech Mahindra Q1 FY27 revenue rose 6.1% YoY to US$1.66bn with operating margin at 14.4%, and deal wins hit US$1.078bn.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 2.2% QoQ and 6.1% YoY in reported USD (6.6% YoY constant currency), with every vertical growing YoY. EBIT margin rose 60 bps QoQ and 330 bps YoY to 14.4%, led by volume growth and Project Fortius savings, partly offset by Comviva seasonality and business mix. Management said Q1 was stronger than expected, helped by early delivery on a European automotive programme that it expects to reverse in Q2. Management reiterated its FY27 ambition of growth above the peer average and an operating margin of 15%, with Q4 margin expected above 15%.

financial_highlights.change: +16.2% YoY in USD; PAT margin +80 bps YoY

segments.name: Communications
segments.commentary: Grew 1.3% YoY; held back by Comviva Q1 seasonality and a cloud pass-through that a client pulled back after a takeover. Management expects the pass-through impact to fade in Q2, and one large deal has not yet ramped.

segments.name: BFSI
segments.commentary: Grew 8.1% YoY and 2.7% QoQ. Acquisition of Avant Techno Solutions (Canada, payments modernisation and wealth platforms) was announced in the quarter.

segments.name: Manufacturing
segments.commentary: Grew 17.2% YoY and 9% QoQ, helped by aerospace and early delivery on a large European automotive programme. Management called the auto delivery acceleration a timing benefit, not a one-off, with a 1%-1.3% revenue pressure expected next quarter.

segments.name: Retail, Travel & Logistics
segments.commentary: Grew 8.6% YoY; management described the macro as mixed.

segments.name: Healthcare (HLS)
segments.commentary: Grew 7.2% YoY and 2.5% QoQ, supported by providers and life sciences; the largest deal wins this quarter came from manufacturing and HLS.

segments.name: Technology, Media & Entertainment
segments.commentary: Declined 1.7% QoQ on continued volatility in client spend. YoY growth was not stated in the call.

guidance_outlook: FY27 target: growth above the peer average (management said it is already ahead in Q1) and an operating margin of 15%; management said Q4 margin must be above 15%.
Q2 growth expected to be supported by ramp-up of large deals won over the past 12 months; the European auto acceleration will create about a 1%-1.3% revenue pressure in Q2.
Wage increases to take effect from Q2 in a phased manner.
Management declined to give a specific FY27 growth number, citing volatility; it said it expects to exceed peer-average growth, by an amount it did not quantify.

Margin levers: Project Fortius (fixed-price productivity, T&M utilisation) and SG&A savings from portfolio company consolidation. Management also flagged wage bill increases and AI-driven productivity pressure as headwinds.
capex_capacity: Communications experience centre in Pune opened in April 2026, with more than 10 executive sessions held in its first two months.
Management said it is investing in centres of excellence in Hyderabad (learning, engineering, retail CPG) and will calibrate investment to growth opportunities.
Investing in talent, IP and software licences; deals are screened to be margin-accretive over the long term.
Headcount in IT services fell 7% YoY because of AI-led productivity gains in fixed-price work. Management expects hiring to resume in the rest of FY27, mixing fresh and experienced talent.
demand_pricing: Deal wins of US$1,078 million, with the largest coming from manufacturing and HLS. Management said the pipeline looks strong but that large deals are binary and hard to forecast beyond a quarter or two.

Demand strengthening in ServiceNow, SAP, Salesforce, and data and AI (Databricks, Snowflake, GenAI). Weakness seen in manual testing, traditional big data, standalone e-commerce, legacy CRM and legacy infrastructure admin.

Management walked away from deals with 70%-80% productivity benefits over 5-7 year contracts and from fixed price guarantees on infrastructure, citing memory and chip price inflation of about 20% YoY.
Auto sector: some customers are cutting costs with AI. Auto finance was resilient. Aerospace demand is rising, especially in IT and engineering.

BPS: AI operations made up most of the BPS deal TCV this quarter, including a large AI-led engagement with a high-tech client. Some clients are questioning in-house versus outsourcing decisions on multi-year deals, but management said it is not seeing outsized delays or cancellations.

qa_highlights.question: Will growth momentum carry into Q2 without the Comviva seasonality?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Q2 to be supported by ramp-up of large deals won over the past 12 months, offset by a European auto slowdown; it expects to meet or exceed the peer-average growth for the full year.

qa_highlights.question: How much margin expansion lever remains, and what is the exit margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give an exit target, but said Q4 margin must be above 15%. Levers are gross margin from Project Fortius plus SG&A gains from portfolio company consolidation. Q1 had seasonal visa and travel costs and Comviva seasonality as negatives.

qa_highlights.question: Is the DSO and free cash flow improvement sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Part of Q1 was helped by accelerated customer payments and FX on receivables, which will normalise. Management said working capital remains a priority with a long-term improvement trend, though quarterly seasonality will persist.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Comms ramp impact is in Q1, and what is the full-year growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: One of the two large Comms deals has not ramped at all yet, so impact comes in later quarters. Management said it would not give a specific full-year growth number, given the volatility.

qa_highlights.question: Was the strong quarter a plan or a surprise, and is demand improving or is share being taken?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the quarter was stronger than expected, helped by the European auto acceleration. It described a shift in demand toward modernisation and platform work, with the core stable and no 'SaaS eclipse' seen; it remains cautiously optimistic.

qa_highlights.question: Given the pricing comparisons with peers, can 15% margins go higher, and what competitor irrationality exists?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 15% is the target for FY27, with a path beyond FY27 to be set. Examples of irrational pricing included 70%-80% productivity assumptions in 5-7 year deals and holding infrastructure prices amid about 20% YoY inflation.

risks_watch: Q2 revenue drag of about 1%-1.3% from the European auto programme acceleration not repeating, plus slower Comms ramp until the large deal goes live.
Wage increase effective Q2 and AI-led productivity pressure on margins, against the 15% FY27 target.
Large-deal conversion is binary; management cannot forecast beyond one or two quarters.
Cash flow and DSO benefits partly from timing (accelerated payments and FX), which management said will normalise.
Auto sector cost pressure and EV programme softness, and client questions about in-house versus outsourced delivery on multi-year deals.
summary.management_tone: Confident on execution and margins, but cautious on the forward view: management declined to give a specific FY27 growth number, citing macro volatility. It was more open about pricing discipline and about the Q2 headwinds from the European auto acceleration and the Comms cloud pass-through.
key_quotes: We had said that in the third year of our transformation, we would pivot strongly to growth, and as the numbers today show, we have done just that.
So it has to be upwards of 15% for the fourth quarter, and we'll see how each quarter progresses from here and now.
So I would feel that the demand situation is not catastrophic.
But candidly, it's not very different from what I used to see, in my 25-plus years in this industry.

adds.what: Communications experience centre in Pune (opened April 2026; experience centre, not productive capacity)

growth.why: Management reiterated FY27 growth above peer average (unquantified, no number given) and a 15% operating margin, with Q4 margin above 15%; delivery backed by large-deal ramp-ups and Project Fortius savings, plus US$1,078m TCV (+33% YoY), but no specific capacity additions and large deals described as binary.
